title: Given an array of non-negative house values, find the maximum amount you can rob without robbing two adjacent houses.
shortTitle: House Robber — cannot rob adjacent houses

s1_definition.profdef: At each house i the best achievable total is the larger of skipping it (carry forward the best up to i−1) or robbing it (its value plus the best up to i−2), giving dp[i] = max(dp[i−1], nums[i] + dp[i−2]). Rolling two variables yields the maximum in linear time and constant space. The adjacency constraint is encoded by reaching back two positions when robbing.
s1_definition.analogy: Think of National Bank of India selecting non-adjacent time slots to run high-value promotions, since two back-to-back slots conflict. At each slot you either skip it and keep your running best, or take it and add it to your best from two slots ago. You keep whichever is larger.
s1_definition.oneliner: For each house take the max of skip (best so far) or rob (value plus best from two back).
s1_definition.raw:
**Professional definition:** At each house i the best achievable total is the larger of skipping it (carry forward the best up to i−1) or robbing it (its value plus the best up to i−2), giving dp[i] = max(dp[i−1], nums[i] + dp[i−2]). Rolling two variables yields the maximum in linear time and constant space. The adjacency constraint is encoded by reaching back two positions when robbing.

**In simple words (banking analogy):** Think of National Bank of India selecting non-adjacent time slots to run high-value promotions, since two back-to-back slots conflict. At each slot you either skip it and keep your running best, or take it and add it to your best from two slots ago. You keep whichever is larger.

**One line to remember:** For each house take the max of skip (best so far) or rob (value plus best from two back).

sections.s2_technical:
Maintain two running bests: the best including up to the previous house and up to the house before that. At each house compute the new best as the larger of carrying the previous best forward or robbing the current house plus the best two houses back. For example: `cur = Math.max(prev1, nums[i] + prev2); prev2 = prev1; prev1 = cur;`.

Robbing the current house forbids the immediately previous one, which is why you add to prev2 (two houses back) rather than prev1. Skipping simply inherits prev1.

The time is O(n) and the space is O(1). A senior nuance is House Robber II, where the houses form a circle so the first and last are adjacent; you solve it by running the linear version twice, once excluding the first house and once excluding the last, and taking the max.
sections.s3_banking:
Problem 1 — At National Bank of India, marketing picks non-adjacent promotional time slots to maximize total value, since consecutive slots would cannibalize each other. This is exactly how House Robber works.

Problem 2 — Choosing a slot rules out the slot immediately before it. This is exactly why robbing adds to the best from two slots back.

The mini-project builds a `PromoSlotOptimizer`, a `BankLogFormatter`, and a runnable demo.

sections.s5_journey:
The input slot values are two, seven, nine, three, one.

Step 1: After slot two the best is two; after slot seven the best is max of two and seven, which is seven.

Step 2: After slot nine the best is max of seven and nine plus two, which is eleven.

Step 3: After slot three the best is max of eleven and three plus seven, which stays eleven.

Step 4: After slot one the best is max of eleven and one plus eleven, which is twelve.

Step 5: The maximum non-adjacent total is twelve, achieved by slots two, nine, and one.

```text
2026-10-27T00:55:00Z [INFO] National Bank of India — Promo Slot Optimizer (House Robber)
2026-10-27T00:55:00Z [INFO] Max non-adjacent promo value = 12
2026-10-27T00:55:00Z [INFO] Best = 12
```


sections.s6_takeaway:
House Robber is a one-dimensional decision DP. At each house I face a binary choice: skip it, in which case my best total is whatever I had through the previous house, or rob it, in which case I earn its value plus my best total from two houses back, because robbing it forbids the immediately adjacent house. The recurrence is dp of i equals the max of dp of i minus one and nums of i plus dp of i minus two.

Since each state depends only on the two preceding bests, I keep two rolling variables rather than an array, giving linear time and constant space. The subtle point that interviewers probe is why robbing reaches back two positions rather than one, and the answer is precisely the adjacency constraint.

In my project at National Bank of India, marketing chose non-adjacent promotional time slots to maximize total value, since consecutive slots would cannibalize each other, and this is structurally identical to House Robber. For the circular case, where the first and last slots are also adjacent, I ran the linear solution twice, once excluding the first slot and once excluding the last, and took the larger result.
